Today's batteries are nothing more than improved Voltaic Piles. Instead of piles of metal pieces, batteries are made up of cells. Cells are single combinations of pile material consisting of two different metals separated by an electrolytic paste or fluid...
The cells can be arranged together in series to provide an increase in voltage, or in parallel to provide an increase in current.
Even the common 9-volt battery is made up of cells. They have six 1.5 volt cells arranged in series.

Adding cells together in series is one way to increase voltage, however, different types of metals and electrolyte combinations will also increase voltage. For example, fully charged nickel-cadmium cells produce about 1.25 volts each, where fully charged lead-acid cells produce around 2.1 volts each...

Batteries are rated by their ability to produce a certain power for a given period of time. This is called the battery's Ampere-Hour (Ah) Rating. A 1 Ah rated battery has the ability to maintain a current flow of 1 ampere for 1 hour...

A 40 Ah rated battery can provide 1 amp for 40 hours, 40 amps for 1 hour, or any combination of amps per hour resulting in 40. If 5 amps are drawn by the load, the battery can provide current for 8 hours...

Notice that the greater the current demand of a battery the less time is available until discharge. That is why aircraft power distribution systems reduce current loads to only essential systems in the event of an aircraft power failure...

The battery servicing area is usually called the Battery Shop. The Lead-Acid and NICAD batteries are not compatible and should never be serviced in the same shop.

It is never a good idea to use the same tools for servicing both Lead-Acid and NICAD batteries due to contamination. If you have no choice, ensure you wash the tools thoroughly with soap and water before use...
Wash the tools thoroughly with soap and water before use.

An eye wash station is a specially designed fixture that flushes the eyes with water in the event that electrolyte comes in contact with the eyes. The eye wash station should be inspected, tested and the water lines purged each month...

Every battery shop must have a fire extinguisher mounted on the wall and free of obstructions. Typically, Halon fire extinguishers are used in battery shops. Never use a CO fire extinguisher to cool an overheated battery. When discharged, CO extinguishers build up static electricity which could result in a spark....

The Constant Current method is used when only a quick topping is required for a capacity check, after the battery has been in storage for an extended period, or as the initial charge after the completion of a deep cycle...

The Constant Potential/Varying Current charging method is used when a discharged battery needs to be fully recharged quickly. This method produces a variable DC voltage above and below the battery voltage. This allows faster charging time and decreased temperature during charging...

The alternating DC voltage is above the battery voltage at high peak and below the battery voltage at low peak. This method is able to inject a large surge of power for approximately one second. The cycle then returns below the battery voltage permitting the battery to discharge slightly for one second...
This action depolarizes the plates and cools the battery. The Constant Potential/Varying Current method charges the battery to maximum capacity in approximately one hour.
The Constant Current method is most effective for topping up batteries.
